paragraphs.text: Long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation (den Boer et al., 2002; Baskin et al., 2010). It usually presents in infancy or early childhood with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, hepatic dysfunction, cardiomyopathy, and hypotonia or myopathy. It may lead to sudden death (Rocchiccioli et al., 1990; Tyni et al., 1997; den Boer et al., 2002). Pigmentary retinopathy and peripheral neuropathy are also features (Bertini et al., 1992; Tyni et al., 1997). Pregnancies with an affected fetus may be complicated by maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy or HELLP syndrome (Wilcken et al., 1993; Ibdah et al., 1999).

paragraphs.text: Rocchiccioli et al. (1990) described a child who presented in early childhood with episodes of coma and hypoglycemia, and with a myopathy and cardiomyopathy that progressed rapidly and led to death at 9 months of age. Ketosis was decreased (blood beta-hydroxybutyrate, 0.07 mmol/L) even though plasma fatty acid levels were normal (0.81 mmol/L). The urine contained excessive amounts of C6 to C10 dicarboxylic acids, and there was an accumulation of medium- and long-chain (C8 to C14) 3-hydroxy-dicarboxylic acids. Studies in cultured fibroblasts showed impaired oxidation of medium- and long-chain fatty acids and deficiency of LCHAD. The activities of long-, medium-, and short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenases and of 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase were normal. The authors noted that the disorder affects the liver, skeletal muscle, and myocardium.

paragraphs.text: Tyni et al. (1997) reported 13 patients with LCHAD deficiency, all homozygous for the G1528C mutation. At presentation the patients had had hypoglycemia, cardiomyopathy, muscle hypotonia, and hepatomegaly during the first 2 years of life. Seven patients had recurrent metabolic crises and 6 had a steadily progressive course. Two patients had cholestatic liver disease, 1 had peripheral neuropathy, and 6 had retinopathy with focal pigmentary aggregations or retinal hypopigmentation. Dicarboxylic aciduria was found in 9 of 10 patients. Most patients had lactic acidosis, increased serum creatine kinase, and low serum carnitine. Three patients had bilateral periventricular or focal cortical lesions on neuroimaging, and 1 had brain atrophy. Only 1 patient, who had received dietary treatment for 9 years, was alive (at age 14 years); all the others died before 2 years of age.

paragraphs.text: Ibdah et al. (1999) found homozygosity for the 1528G-C (E474Q) mutation in a patient with LCHAD deficiency who presented with infantile hypocalcemia and cholestasis. The patient's mother had preeclampsia in that pregnancy and acute fatty liver of pregnancy in a later one.

checks.claim: A patient with LCHAD deficiency was homozygous for the HADHA 1528G-C (E474Q) mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Molecular analysis revealed homozygosity for the prevalent LCHAD (1528G > C, E474Q) mutation.
checks.explanation: HADHA is the standard symbol for the LCHAD gene.

checks.claim: The patient with LCHAD deficiency homozygous for HADHA E474Q presented with infantile hypocalcemia.
checks.evidence_quote: The proband presented at 2 months of age with an acute infantile hypocalcaemia

checks.claim: The patient with LCHAD deficiency homozygous for HADHA E474Q presented with cholestasis.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with occult, unexplained cholestatic liver disease

checks.claim: The mother of the LCHAD-deficient patient homozygous for HADHA E474Q had preeclampsia during the pregnancy with that patient.
checks.evidence_quote: The mother had pre-eclampsia during the third trimester of her pregnancy.

checks.claim: The mother of the LCHAD-deficient patient homozygous for HADHA E474Q had acute fatty liver of pregnancy in a later pregnancy.
checks.evidence_quote: In a subsequent pregnancy, she developed severe acute fatty liver of pregnancy (AFLP)

paragraphs.text: Baskin et al. (2010) found homozygosity for this mutation, designated c.1526G-C (p.Glu510Gln), in a child with LCHAD deficiency. The child had inherited it through paternal uniparental isodisomy of chromosome 2.

checks.claim: A child with LCHAD deficiency was homozygous for the HADHA mutation designated c.1526G-C (p.Glu510Gln).
checks.evidence_quote: the child was homozygous for the common mutation, c.1526G > C (p.Glu510Gln) in the HADHA gene

checks.claim: The child with LCHAD deficiency inherited homozygosity for HADHA c.1526G-C (p.Glu510Gln) through paternal uniparental isodisomy of chromosome 2.
checks.evidence_quote: Short tandem repeat testing with markers covering both short and long arms of chromosome 2 showed that the child has paternal uniparental isodisomy.
checks.explanation: The abstract and title support inheritance through paternal isodisomy of chromosome 2.

paragraphs.text: Sims et al. (1995) found a C1132T mutation in the HADHA gene in a child with LCHAD deficiency whose mother had acute fatty liver of pregnancy. The mutation creates a premature termination codon at residue 342. The child carried G1528C on the other allele and was therefore compound heterozygous.

checks.claim: A child with LCHAD deficiency carried a C1132T mutation in the HADHA gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The third child had this G1528C mutation on one allele and a different mutation (C1132T) creating a premature termination codon (residue 342) on the second allele.

checks.claim: The mother of the child with LCHAD deficiency carrying HADHA C1132T had acute fatty liver of pregnancy.
checks.evidence_quote: In all families, the mothers had acute fatty liver and associated sever complications during pregnancies with the affected infants.
checks.explanation: Applies to all 3 families, including this child's.

checks.claim: The HADHA C1132T mutation creates a premature termination codon at residue 342.

checks.claim: The child with LCHAD deficiency carrying HADHA C1132T carried the G1528C mutation on the other allele and was therefore compound heterozygous.
checks.evidence_quote: The third child had this G1528C mutation on one allele and a different mutation (C1132T) creating a premature termination codon (residue 342) on the second allele.
checks.explanation: Compound heterozygous for G1528C and C1132T.
